scenes.question: When does the burning season open, peak and close?

beats.say: Think of a cricket match. When does it really start? When the first ball is bowled? A fairer answer might be when ten percent of the runs are scored. And it is basically over when ninety percent are on the board.

Formula twenty-nine, season start, peak and end, uses the same idea. Within a declared window, the season starts when ten percent of the detected activity has happened, ends at ninety percent, and peaks in the busiest week.

parts.say: S of w is the running total, up to week w. Think of a bucket filling up as the season goes on.

It adds up c u, the fire cell-days of every week u, up to and including week w. The start is the first week where S passes ten percent of the season's total. The end is where it passes ninety percent. One consistent sensor is used for all years, VIIRS S-NPP from 2012.

And w only runs inside a declared window, from t a to t b. For the rice-residue season in Punjab and Haryana, that is the fifteenth of September to the thirty-first of December. A week without observation makes the whole year unknown.

steps.label: Start, 2025 · 10% reached
steps.say: In 2025, ten percent of the season's cell-days had happened by the thirteenth of October. That is the start.

steps.label: Peak, 2025 · busiest week
steps.say: The busiest week was the week of the third of November. That is the peak.

steps.label: End, 2025 · 90% reached
steps.say: And ninety percent was reached by the thirtieth of November. That is the end. The season held 4,010 cell-days in the window, down from 18,231 in 2016. These are dates of detected activity, which is what satellites can tell us.

scenes.title: The kharif burning season, year by year

beats.say: For each year, the bar runs from the ten percent week to the ninety percent week of VIIRS S-NPP fire cell-days, in the window from mid-September to the end of December. The dot marks the busiest week.

The timing is remarkably stable: opening in the first half of October, closing in the second half of November. But in the most recent years the end has moved a week later, and the peak towards early November.

beats.label: Season-by-season chart
beats.say: On the FIREWORK website, open the Calendar and scroll to the season-by-season chart. It lets you follow each burning season through the months, year after year.

beats.label: Month × year grid
beats.say: In the grid above it, you can see the season's shape too: the October and November squares light up every year. A late end matters, because the colder weeks of November trap smoke more easily.

points: Start = 10% of the window's activity, end = 90%

beats.say: So, to remember: fill the bucket week by week inside a fixed window, and read where it passes ten and ninety percent. It turns the calendar into a schedule that farmers, regulators and health agencies can use.
